outcomes.reasoning: The review flags the same line (backfill.mjs:119). It says Branch: must be present to parse but is only optionally emitted, so claims without a branch can never be backfilled. That is the same underlying defect.

The review covers the same race, a competing claim arriving around the write, but calls the resulting verification failure a false alarm and suggests checking against the pre-write claim. The defect is that the stale claim gets written to Project fields without revalidation during the batch, which the review never identifies.

The review raises two unrelated points: C1 control characters are not rejected, and a one-line wrapper should be inlined. It never mentions the race where a newer claim arrives during the write batch.

The review cites the same doc lines, but its concern is that a multi-paragraph note silently kills the claim parsing. It says nothing about the Claim ID code span being broken mid-token or the lost list indentation.

The review describes a parse failure caused by a missing Branch: line when the branch is falsy. The defect is about trailing blank lines after the handoff text failing the bounded-handoff check. Both end in the same readSnapshot error, but the root causes differ.

The review flags a different parse failure: a claim comment with no Branch line is rejected. It does not mention a trailing newline or blank line after the handoff sentence that fails the non-empty line check.

The review is about a claim comment that has no Branch: line and a misleading error. Defect 1 is a trailing newline after the handoff footer being rejected by the non-empty-line check. The problems differ, even though both touch the same parser.
